STATUTORY AUTHORITY & DISCLAIMER This is a SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS conducted pursuant to RFO Part 10 (Market Research). This notice is issued solely for informational and planning purposes; it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or Request for Quotation (RFQ). This notice does not commit the U.S. Government (USG) to contract for any supply or service. The Government will not award a contract based on this Sources Sought, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing or submitting responses. Participation is strictly voluntary. Failure to respond to this announcement will not preclude an interested party from submitting an offer under any subsequent formal solicitation, should one be issued. Information received will be used within the Department of the Air Force to determine market capabilities, potential small-business set-aside opportunities, and procurement strategy. 3. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT The 354th Contracting Squadron (354 CONS) at Eielson AFB, Alaska, is conducting market research to identify qualified, capable, and certified commercial contractors interested in providing on-call, critical emergency and scheduled maintenance and repair services for the Central Heat and Power Plant (CHPP) high-pressure power boilers. A copy of the draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) is attached to this SAM.gov posting as Attachment 1. Vendors are strongly advised to review Attachment 1 in its entirety prior to responding. 3.1 Background & Plant Criticality The Eielson AFB CHPP provides vital thermal heat and electrical power to all base facilities under extreme sub-arctic winter conditions (temperatures regularly dropping below -40�F). Unplanned boiler outages pose immediate life-safety, mission, and infrastructure failure risks. Consequently, repair response times and quality standards are non-negotiable. 3.2 Equipment Inventory The requirement encompasses six (6) utility-grade, coal-fired high-pressure power boilers and their associated support systems: Four (4) Springfield Boiler Co. Model #1951 coal-fired high-pressure boilers. Two (2) Indeck Keystone Energy Model #2013 coal-fired high-pressure boilers. 3.3 Core Performance Scope (Refer to PWS Sections 1.0 � 2.5) The contractor shall provide all management, personnel, labor, transportation, tooling, equipment, and certified materials to perform: 24-Hour Emergency Physical On-Site Response: A qualified technician must be physically present on-site at Eielson AFB within 24 hours of initial call-out notification from the Contracting Officer (CO) or Contracting Officer�s Representative (COR). On-Site Inspection & Letter of Recommended Repair (LRR): Submission of a detailed LRR (including root cause, part numbers, compliance citations, labor hours, lead times, and a firm-fixed-price proposal) within one (1) business day of inspection. CO Notice-to-Proceed (NTP) Enforcement: No parts ordering or work beyond initial inspection may occur without formal written authorization from the Contracting Officer. Full Boiler Envelope & Pressure Vessel Repair: Extensive repairs to include any and all associated piping related to boiler production but not limited to: welding, rolling, reshaping, and replacement of water wall tubes, superheater tubes, economizer tubes, generating tubes, pier tubes, front/sidewall/rear headers, superheater headers, mud drums, steam drums, power piping, blowdown drains, safety valves, hand holes, manholes, soot blowers, baffles, and gas passes. No Government-Furnished Property (GFE/GFP): The Government will furnish zero tools, vehicles, facilities, tube rollers, or welding equipment (PWS Section 4.4). Base Security & HAZMAT: Personnel must be vetted via the Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) and satisfy Bioenvironmental Engineering SDS/HAZMAT approval processes prior to bringing materials on-site. 4. MANDATORY QUALIFICATION THRESHOLDS To be deemed capable under this requirement, respondents must demonstrate compliance with the following mandatory qualifications (see PWS Section 3.0): ASME "R" Stamp: The prime contractor must hold an active National Board "R" (Repairs and Alterations) Stamp Certificate of Authorization. ASME Section IX Welder Certifications: All personnel executing welding and repair tasks must hold current certifications compliant with ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code Section IX. State of Alaska Boiler Inspection: All repairs must be inspected and formally accepted by a certified State of Alaska Boiler Inspector. The contractor is solely responsible for scheduling and funding these inspections prior to invoice submittal. Part II: Industry Feedback & PWS Comments Identify any ambiguities, restrictive requirements, or commercial standard misalignments in the attached draft PWS (Attachment 1). Provide feedback on proposed NAICS classification and potential subcontracting/teaming arrangements 5. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Format: Electronic submission in Adobe PDF format via email. Due Date & Time: All responses must be received no later than 10/30/2026 at 16:00 AKST. title: Marine Corps Intense Cold Weather Combat Boot
description: This procurement is for the manufacture and delivery of Boots, Intense Cold Weather Marine Corps Combat (MC ICWB) PGC#03939. The MC ICWB will be procured in accordance with purchase description MC/PD-23-01 dated 15 December 2023. The solicitation will have one (1) lot for a 100% of total requirement and be issued as 100% Small Business Set-Aside Competition after Exclusion of Sources, FAR 6.203 Set-asides for small business concerns. The solicitation will be evaluated under Best Value Trade-Off Source Selection Procedures with the following evaluation factors: (1) Product Demonstration Models (PDM), and (2) Past Performance Confidence Assessment. Offerors are required to include Product Demonstration Models (PDMs). Evaluation will consist of PDM, Past Performance, and price. All evaluation factors other than cost or price, when combined, are significantly more important than cost or price. As other evaluation factors become more equal, the evaluated cost or price becomes more important. Quantities: This procurement contains a three (3) year base term. Within the three year base term there will be three (3) 12-month price tier periods. The Minimum Quantity is 1,260 pairs for the life of the resultant contract. The Minimum Quantity may be ordered during any tier period or combination of tier periods. The Government may fulfill the Minimum Quantity by issuing a single delivery order or any number of delivery orders. However, in fulfilling the Minimum Quantity, the total dollar value expended by the Government shall not exceed the dollar value of the Minimum Quantity procured at the lowest unit price under the contract, hereafter referred to as the �Guaranteed Minimum Dollar Value.� The Government will be considered to have fulfilled its obligation to order the Minimum Quantity when the Guaranteed Minimum Dollar Value has been met. The Annual Estimated Quantity (AEQ) is 5,000 (Tier 1)/5,000 (Tier 2)/5,000 (Tier 3). The Maximum Quantity is 22,500 pairs and reflects the sum of approximately 1.50% of the AEQ for each Tier period (a total of 3 Tiers) to account for fluctuations in customer demand. The Government reserves the right to place orders up to the Maximum Contract Quantity. The Government is not obligated to order the Contract Maximum Quantity; however, the Government has the legal right to order up to this quantity prior to the final expiration of any resultant contract. The result contract will be a Firm-Fixed Price, Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract type. The Production Lead Time is 180 days first delivery order and 150 days for subsequent delivery orders. Inspection/Acceptance at Origin. Destination will be at VSTZ - Travis - Austin, TX, DoDAAC # SD0131: Travis Association for the Blind AF & MC 3PL -Distribution Services 4512 South Pleasant Valley Road Austin, Texas 78744. Important Notices: The Government reserves the right to perform conversions to the Boot, Marine Corps Combat Intense Cold Weather with a similar construction item(s) due to military readiness requirements to support uniform changes. Any conversion will be via bilateral modification. description: Facilities Operations, Maintenance and Support Services for U.S. EPA Facilities at Research Triangle Park (RTP), North Carolina The United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Research Triangle Park (RTP) Facilities located at 109 T.W. Alexander Drive, RTP, NC 27711 has a requirement for facilities, maintenance and support services. The Government anticipates the award of a Firm Fixed Priced type contract (with a fixed price redetermination retrospective contract line item, a cost reimbursement contract line item and three IDIQ line items) with a twelve-month base period and four (4) twelve-month option periods. The EPA's facilities on the RTP Campus consists of 1.3 million square feet of offices, laboratories, computer and conference spaces, and child care facilities. The EPA RTP facilities are classified as a Centers for Disease Control (CDC) Bio- Safety Level II Research Facility and AAALAC (Association for Assessment and Accreditation of Laboratory Animal care International) facilities. The purpose is to provide facilities operations, maintenance and support services for the U.S. EPA RTP facilities on a twenty-four hour, seven days a week basis. The Contractor shall provide all management, training, licensed personnel, tools, and labor necessary to perform all functions, operations, and tasks, in accordance with all applicable industry performance standards, to include but not be limited to, National, state and local codes; OSHA regulations; Federal specifications; EPA facility standards; and EPA-RTP policies and procedures. The Contractor shall establish, implement, and maintain facilities management services that are responsive to the Government�s stewardship. The Contractor is expected to maintain an acute awareness of the quality, efficiency, and cost effectiveness of all services to be provided with a continuing emphasis on devising and developing better methods and/or procedures to enhance the ability of OCSFO-RTP to meet the needs of its clients. The Government envisions the O&M Contract to be divided into three (3) primary areas and consists of Base Contract Requirements, Standing Task Orders, and Task Orders. The Fixed Priced Base Contract requirements include all routine and predictable services such as Building Automation System operations, Facility Trouble Desk, Administrative Support, Program Management Support, Key Personnel, Quality Management, and the Preventative Maintenance Program. The ID/IQ efforts on the contract are issued via task orders for the required services, subject to the Service Contract Labor Standards (SCLS) / Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) or for construction services subject to the Construction Wage Rate Requirements Statute (CWRRS). description: Title: Shipyard Infrastructure Optimization Program Multi-Mission Dry Dock, Multiple Award Construction Contract Type: Pre-Solicitation Notice Location: Primarily at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS & IMF), located at Naval Base Kitsap (NBK) Bremerton, Washington and other areas under the cognizance of Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) Pacific. Solicitation Method: NAVFAC intends to issue one (1) solicitation in September 2026 that results in the award of approximately five (5) Indefinite-Delivery Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) Multiple Award Construction Contracts (MACC) primarily in support of the Shipyard Infrastructure Optimization Program (SIOP) Multi-Mission Dry Dock. Solicitation and award of the MACC is anticipated to utilize single phase (one-step) Design-Build (DB) selection procedures. Anticipated Evaluation Factors: Anticipated non-cost/price and price evaluation factors for the solicitation are summarized as follows: Factor 1 � Technical Approach (acceptable/unacceptable) Factor 2 � Experience Factor 3 � Past Performance Factor 4 � Small Business Utilization and Participation Factor 5 � Safety (acceptable/unacceptable) Price NOTE: The Government anticipates that evaluation of Factor 2 � Experience will encompass relevant projects for BOTH construction projects AND design projects. Period of Performance/Maximum Value: The period of performance is anticipated to be a base period of 5-years and one (1) 5-year option period for a maximum possible duration of 10-years; or an aggregate maximum estimated value of $15,000,000,000 for all task orders, whichever occurs first. NAICS Codes: This MACC will encompass a wide range of DB and Design-Bid-Build (DBB) type projects primarily representative of North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) codes 237990 (primary) Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction as well as 236220 (secondary) Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. Task Order Range: The typical size of major construction task orders will range from $2,000,000,000 to $6,000,000,000; however, smaller task orders may be issued to support smaller efforts such as Early Contractor Involvement (ECI) and/or Alternative Technical Concepts (ATC). Task orders may be above this limit; however, contractors are not obligated to accept such task orders under the general terms of the contract. For evaluation purposes, the Government anticipates that the solicitation may stipulate that construction projects with a minimum value of $500,000,000 will be deemed relevant. The Navy anticipates that most work under the MACC will be initiated by task order(s) that are competed amongst all the MACC holders (firms awarded one of the potential contracts). Additionally, all MACC holders may be issued task orders for the same scope of work for ECI and/or ATC or where justified, task order awards may be issued to a single MACC holder. The Navy makes no representation as to the number of task orders or actual amount of work to be ordered; however, each MACC holder is anticipated to receive a minimum guarantee in the amount of $1,000,000. As subsequent task orders are awarded which exceed the $1,000,000 minimum guarantee, the $1,000,000 minimum guarantee will be de-obligated and the Government�s obligation for the minimum guarantee for the contract will be satisfied. Bonding Capacity: To qualify for this MACC, the Government anticipates that the solicitation may stipulate that Offerors will need to demonstrate single project bonding capacity of $1,000,000,000 and an aggregate bonding capacity of $3,000,000,000. Acquisition Timeline (Anticipated): Industry Day: 20 August 2026 (actual) Issue MACC Solicitation: 30 September 2026 MACC Pre-Proposal Conference: October 2026 MACC Proposals Due: December 2026 MACC Award: June 2027 Issue Alternative Technical Concept (ATC) Task Order(s): June 2027 ATC Proposals Due (Initial): August 2027 ATC Proposals Due (Final): November 2027 RFP Task Order Marine Package #1: November-December 2027 Planned task order award of Marine Package #1: June 2028 Purpose and Scope: The focus of this MACC will be the construction of a new proposed Multi-Mission Dry Dock in support of SIOP requirements at PSNS & IMF, located at NBK Bremerton, Washington. The Multi-Mission Dry Dock preferred location is within the existing Dry Dock 3 footprint, existing Pier 6, and existing Pier 7; and will include dry dock drainage, dewatering, and flooding systems; a caisson; roadways and rail networks; portal crane track; access and egress elements; mechanical, electrical, and communications systems; support buildings; and utility routing tunnels. The proposed project also includes demolition of facilities and utilities. The Multi-Mission Dry Dock is a fully pressure-relieved dry dock capable of accommodating shipyard repair services for the newest Ford-class aircraft carrier, Nimitz-class carriers, and other surface and subsurface ships served by PSNS & IMF. Dredging south of Multi-Mission Dry Dock is proposed for the Double-Wall Cofferdams, which provides means to support construction of Multi-Mission Dry Dock in the dry, and provides hydraulic cutoff in the permanent condition. The bathymetry in Sinclair Inlet provides adequate water depths to support the drafts of the respective design vessels at berth and during docking/undocking evolutions. Site access is anticipated to be a combination of a temporary fixed pier southeast of existing Building 460, a contractor access road at Bremerton Gate, existing Piers 6 & 7, Dry Dock 3, and the South Gate vehicle inspection building. Prior to establishing the above-described entry points the Navy requires the contractor to install a temporary Controlled Industrial Area (CIA) fence that will encompass the project site. For more information on the proposed Multi-Mission Dry Dock project see: https://bremertonwaterfrontimprovementseis.com/ https://multimissiondrydock.com/ Potential Risk Mitigations: The Navy is considering the following risk mitigation measures including but not limited to: Early Contractor Involvement (ECI) Economic Price Adjustment (EPA) Award Fee and/or Schedule Incentive Reduced small business subcontracting targets One or more of the items under this acquisition may be subject to Free Trade Agreements or the World Trade Organization Government Procurement Agreement. title: Germany – Pharmaceutical products – Abschluss nicht exkl. Arzneimittel-Rabattvereinb. nach § 130a Abs. 8 SGB V im Wege eines Open-House-Modells zum Wirkstoff Glyceroltrinitrat (ATC-Code nach WHO: C05AE01)
description: Gegenstand dieser Veröffentlichung ist der Abschluss nicht exklusiver Rabattvereinbarungen nach § 130a Abs. 8 SGB V über Arzneimittel mit dem Wirkstoff Glyceroltrinitrat (ATC-Code nach WHO: C05AE01). Der Vertragsabschluss erfolgt im Rahmen eines sog. Open-House-Modells, d. h. ein Vertragsabschluss steht innerhalb des Teilnahmezeitraums allen interessierten pharmazeutischen Unternehmen offen, sofern diese die Teilnahmevoraussetzungen erfüllen und akzeptieren. Dies hat zur Folge, dass individuelle Vertragsverhandlungen nicht geführt werden und eine (Liefer-)Exklusivität nicht gegeben ist. Es wird darauf hingewiesen, dass die Abnahmemenge unbekannt ist, da diese von der Nachfrage und der Entwicklung der Versichertenzahl, von dem Verordnungsverhalten der Ärzte sowie dem Abgabe- und Bevorratungsverhalten der öffentlichen Apotheken abhängig ist. Mindestabnahmemengen werden demensprechend nicht garantiert. Interessierte pharmazeutische Unternehmer können die Teilnahmeunterlagen über den Projektraum des Deutschen Vergabeportals (DTVP) herunterladen. Dazu ist zunächst ein Antrag auf Zugang zum Projektraum erforderlich. Nach erfolgter Freischaltung durch die Auftraggeberin kann anschließend auf die Teilnahmeunterlagen zugegriffen werden. Über den Inhalt der Teilnahmeunterlagen - insbesondere über den Inhalt der Rabattvereinbarung und den dort genannten Rabatten - ist absolutes Stillschweigen zu bewahren. Eine vollständige oder teilweise Weitergabe oder Zugänglichmachung von Inhalten der Teilnahmeunterlagen an bzw. für Dritte bedarf der vorherigen schriftlichen Zustimmung der Auftraggeberin. Sofern von einer Teilnahme abgesehen wird, sind alle Unterlagen unverzüglich datenschutzgerecht zu vernichten. Die einzureichenden Unterlagen ergeben sich aus den im Projektraum hinterlegten Dokumenten "Anschreiben" und "Erläuterungen der Vertragsbedingungen". Die Kommunikation, einschließlich der Übermittlung der Teilnahmeunterlagen, erfolgt elektronisch über das Vergabeportal DTVP; Einzelheiten hierzu sind den zuvor genannten Dokumenten zu entnehmen. Etwaige anderslautende Angaben in der Auftragsbekanntmachung sind technischen Gründen geschuldet und beanspruchen keine Verbindlichkeit. Teilnahmeanträge können für einen Vertragsbeginn zum 01.08.2025 erstmals bis zum 23.06.2025 eingereicht werden. Die für einen Vertragsbeginn (ab dem 01.09.2025 oder später) geltenden Einreichungsfristen entnehmen Sie bitte der im Projektraum hinterlegten Anlage "Einreichungsfristen". Fällt der Tag der Einreichungsfrist auf einen Sonnabend, Sonntag oder bundesweit gesetzlichen Feiertag, so tritt an die Stelle eines solchen Tages der nächste Werktag. Bei verspätetem Zugang werden die eingereichten Teilnahmeanträge zur nächsten Einreichungsfrist berücksichtigt. Die Rabattvereinbarung endet, unabhängig vom Datum des Vertragsschlusses, spätestens zum 31.10.2026. Die Auftraggeberin behält sich vor, das Open-House-Verfahren vorzeitig zu beenden, insbesondere im Falle des Abschlusses exklusiver Rabattvereinbarungen; in diesem Fall enden die bereits geschlossenen Rabattvereinbarungen nach Maßgabe der vertraglichen Bestimmungen. Den Erfahrungen der Auftraggeberin nach treten exklusive Rabattvereinbarungen in der Regel 8 bis 12 Monate nach der Veröffentlichung der entsprechenden Auftragsbekanntmachung im Supplement zum Amtsblatt der Europäischen Union in Kraft.

title: Notice of Intent to Single Source- Construction Surveillance Technicians
description: The 35th Contracting Squadron, Misawa Air Base, Japan has conducted market research and intends to solicit, negotiate and award a single source firm-fixed price (FFP) purchase order under the authority of RFO 12.102(a) to a small business: Lavish Life Technologies LLC UEI CR8FCJQP2747. The proposed North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 561612, with a small business size of $29,000,000.00. This purchase order will be a follow-on contract to contract FA520525P0071 to purchase Construction Surveillance Technician Services needed to complete iFortress facility and its follow-on accreditation. The services being acquired will be critical to ensuring this construction project comply with the requirements defined in the Intelligence Community Directive (ICD) 705, "Physical and Technical Security Standards for Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIF)", and the Department of Defense (DoD) 5105.21-M-Volumes 1,2,3, "Sensitive Compartmented Information Administrative Security Manual", dated October 2012. This is a single source award due to the ability to leverage existing Construction Surveillance Technicians already deployed to Misawa under the current contract. Awarding a follow-on contract will cut mobilization costs and prevent further project delays. Based on market research it takes 30 days or more for the mobilization of new staff after sourcing and onboarding employee. The Hawaii National Guard intends to issue a Request for Proposals (RFP) to award a single firm fixed-price contract for services, non-personal, to provide all plant, labor, transportation, materials, tools, equipment, appliances and supervision necessary for the Construction of KNMD209085 Munitions Maintenance and Inspection Facility and KNMD209086 Conventional Munitions Cube Storage Addition located on the Hawaii Air National Guard campus, at Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam (JBPHH), Hawaii. These projects will be concurrent. KNMD209085 Munitions Maintenance and Inspection Facility - Construct a new Munitions Maintenance and Inspections facility by utilizing conventional design and construction methods to accommodate the facility mission. This project has a statutory cost limitation $14M for Unspecified Minor Military Construction (UMMC) Project - Adjustment of Dollar Limitations for Location pursuant to 10 USC Section 2805. Project square footage is estimated at 2,400 SF. Work covered in this project includes but is not limited to: Micro-pile Foundations: Specialized foundation engineering featuring micro-piles to mitigate challenging soil conditions and ensure seismic structural integrity. Cast-in-Place Concrete: Constructing robust concrete slab-on-grade, concrete walls, capping beams, and associated structural masonry elements. Structural Framing and Enclosure: Utilizing cold-formed metal framing, insulated metal wall panels, and structural steel support systems. Roofing: Installation of high-performance standing seam metal roofing, complete with prefinished gutters, downspouts, and weather barrier wraps. Specialized Systems: Installation of mechanical HVAC systems (including specialized 20-ton air conditioning systems), interior plumbing, lightning/grounding protection, and communication infrastructure. Fire Protection: A complete fire alarm-mass notification system and wet-pipe sprinkler suppression system. In addition to the base work described above, the solicitation will include the following option line items: 1. MAC Pad - Construct 1,167 SY concrete pad for the Material Assembly Center (MAC), required for constructing munitions, along with new asphalt pavement for access and egress to the facility maintenance bays. KNMD209086 Conventional Munitions Cube Storage Addition - Construct an addition to the Munitions Cube Storage Facility (B3552) utilizing conventional design and construction methods to support the F-22 mission. This project has a statutory cost limitation $14M for Unspecified Minor Military Construction (UMMC) Project - Adjustment of Dollar Limitations for Location pursuant to 10 USC Section 2805. Project square footage is estimated at 1,320 SF. Work covered in this project includes but is not limited to: Substructure and Enclosure: Micro-pile foundations, concrete wall structures, cast-in-place concrete slabs, and 12 in. thick concrete walls designed for high-hazard storage specifications. Framing and Roofing: Structural steel framing, roof joists, and standing seam metal roofing matching existing facility standards. Exterior Elements: Erection of new asphalt pavement adjacent to the existing facility access to provide adequate logistics and material handling access around the new facility addition. Specialized Protection: Maintenance facility lightning and grounding protection systems, along with integrated fire detection and alarm reporting systems connected back to the base reporting system. APPLICABLE TO BOTH PROJECTS: RAB Lighting exterior wall packs and area lights are sole source/brand name specific for compatibility with existing installation systems (noted justifications will be included with solicitation). Project Phasing and Security Gates: The contractor will be required to erect a temporary security fence around the construction zone in accordance with the project staging and phasing drawings. Escort Requirements: Escort personnel shall be required when erecting the temporary security fence, performing work occurring outside the temporary security fence, and connecting utilities to the existing system. Secured Zone Access: Once the temporary security fencing is approved and accepted by the Contracting Officers Representative (COR), no escort shall be required within the active secured work zone during construction, allowing the contractor to work within the secured boundary unimpeded. The magnitude of construction is between $10,000,000 and $25,000,000 total. title: Request for Information (RFI): Identifying the Next Generation of NSF X-Labs Topics
description: The U.S. National Science Foundation (NSF), Directorate for Technology, Innovation and Partnerships (TIP), is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to obtain public input on scientific and technological opportunities that could become future topics for the NSF X-Labs Initiative. NSF seeks information on high impact platform technology opportunities, critical technical bottlenecks, enabling infrastructure, potential partnerships, and conditions under which dedicated X-Labs teams could accelerate scientific and technological breakthroughs. This RFI is for planning and information gathering purposes only. It is not a solicitation, funding opportunity, or request for proposals, and NSF will not make an award based on responses to this RFI. Responses are due October 30, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET.

description: INTRODUCTION Battelle Energy Alliance, LLC (BEA) Management & Operating Contractor of the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) owned Idaho National Laboratory (INL), is seeking an Expression of Interest (EOI) from qualified vendors to provide refurbishment services for the Fiber Dial Room and implement point-to-point fiber connectivity upgrades. This initiative supports BEA�s commitment to maintaining robust and reliable communications infrastructure across INL facilities. BACKGROUND The Fiber Dial Room requires refurbishment and modernization to support enhanced fiber optic connectivity and point-to-point communication capabilities. The scope of work may include the following: Refurbishment of the Fiber Dial Room, including structural and environmental improvements. Installation and configuration of point-to-point fiber connections. Integration with existing network infrastructure and systems. Compliance with DOE cybersecurity, safety, and operational standards. Testing and documentation to ensure full functionality and reliability. INL is a U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) national laboratory dedicated to nuclear energy, national security, and clean energy innovation. INL is operated under a management and operating contract with the Department of Energy and as such, the Davis-Bacon Act applies for contracts in excess of $2,000 for the construction, alteration, or repair (including painting and decorating) of buildings or works at INL. Construction work at the laboratory Site covered under the Davis-Bacon Act is additionally subject to the INL Site Stabilization Agreement (SSA). These Site areas include all areas within the 890-square mile boundary, including the Material and Fuels Complex, Central Facilities Area, Advanced Test Reactor, Radioactive Waste Management Complex, and Specific Manufacturing Capability. The agreement is between signatory contractors and labor unions performing such work. Information regarding the INL Site Stabilization Agreement is available from the Site Labor Coordinator at (208) 524-4404 or at lance@sitelabor.org. Construction work performed at Idaho Falls facilities is not subject to these agreements. PROCESS This EOI is the first step in identifying interested and qualified vendors. Responses may be used to inform the development of a formal solicitation list. Selected vendors may be invited to participate in a Request for Proposal (RFP) process for award consideration. SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS Interested vendors should submit an Expression of Interest that includes the following: Company name and point of contact Description of relevant fiber installation and refurbishment capabilities and experience NAICS codes and business size classification Any existing DOE or federal contracting experience (if applicable) Deadline for submission: October 30, 2026 Submit to: Chase.Egbert@inl.gov Only select respondents, as determined by BEA, will receive an invitation to participate in the anticipated RFP solicitation. PROPRIETARY INFORMATION Because information received in response to this EOI may be business sensitive or proprietary to the responding party, respondents must mark information in their responses accordingly.

description: Im Rahmen des Projekts „Errichtung Großwärmespeicher und dessen hydraulische Einbindung in die Fernwärmeverteilung am Standort HKW West“ (Gesamtprojekt WSPW) der Stadtwerke Karlsruhe soll ein Wärmespeicher zur Sicherstellung einer nachhaltigen, zukunftsfähigen und gesicherten Wärmeversorgung realisiert werden. Die verfahrenstechnische Aufgabe des zu planenden 2-Zonen-Wärmespeichers soll in der Speicherung und bedarfsgerechten Bereitstellung thermischer Energie innerhalb des Fernwärmesystems bestehen. Der drucklos ausgeführte Wärmespeicher soll durch die Ausbildung einer thermischen Schichtung die getrennte Aufnahme und Abgabe von Wärme auf unterschiedlichen Temperaturniveaus ermöglichen. Durch die hydraulisch entkoppelte Einbindung in das Fernwärmenetz über ein separates Vor- und Rücklaufsystem soll der Wärmespeicher zum Ausgleich von Lastschwankungen sowie zur zeitlichen Entkopplung von Wärmeerzeugung und -verbrauch beitragen. Bei diesem Beschaffungsvorhaben sollen funktionstüchtige Vor- und Rücklauf- sowie Beimischpumpen einschließlich aller zum bestimmungsgemäßen Betrieb erforderlichen Komponenten innerhalb der spezifizierten Liefergrenzen geplant, hergestellt und geliefert werden.

title: Ireland – Construction work for electricity power lines – The MaresConnect 750MW HVDC Interconnector System
description: The MaresConnect Project is a proposed 750 MW, 320 kV High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) electricity interconnector linking Denbighshire, Wales and North County Dublin, Ireland. Developed by MaresConnect Limited, a joint venture between Foresight Group Holdings Ltd and Etchea Energy Nominees Ltd, the project will transmit electricity via approximately 240 km of subsea and underground cables between new converter stations on each side. It aims to enhance security of supply, market integration, and renewable energy utilisation between the Irish and GB grids. MaresConnect shall utilise Voltage Source Converter (VSC) technology and the configuration shall be a Symmetrical Monopole. The rated DC voltage shall be +/-320 kV. The link shall be bi-directional and shall have a rated power (receiving end) of 750 MW. The project is being procured as separate EPC (Turnkey) contracts, divided into four lots: LOT 1A: EPC for two HVDC Converter Stations; LOT 1B: EPC for one Irish 400kV AC Tail Substation; LOT 2A: EPC for the HVDC subsea and underground cable system, and for the HVAC underground cable system in Wales (Bodelwyddan); LOT 2B: EPC for the supply and installation of HVAC cable system in Ireland (Dublin). The contract model for the lots will be amended FIDIC Conditions of Contract for EPC/Turnkey Projects (Silver Book). MaresConnect has conducted Preliminary Market Engagement prior to publication of this Contract Notice and encourages further collaboration between OEMs and Construction Contractors to establish bidding arrangements in time for the next step of the Procurement Process (notably the Pre-Qualification Questionnaire).

description: PRESOLICITATION NOTICE The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) intends to issue a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for a sequencing facility to conduct de novo epigenetic methylation clock development for the Mojave Desert tortoise using whole-genome enzymatic methylation and 5-base workflow, including the preparation and sequencing of DNA samples for methylation analysis, delivery of sequencing data, and de novo epigenetic methylation clock development. The objective is to generate data and identify loci that will be used to age tortoises. The Government anticipates awarding a firm-fixed-price purchase order for these services. Service Contract Act (SCA) is applicable and the wage determination corresponding to the location of performance will apply. ACQUISITION PROCEDURES This acquisition will be conducted using the simplified procedures for commercial products and commercial services under RFO Part 12. In accordance with RFO 12.201-1(c)(2), for acquisitions at or below the Simplified Acquisition Threshold, the Contracting Officer may solicit quotations directly from suppliers. When using direct solicitation procedures, the Government will: 1. Post a presolicitation notice in the Governmentwide Point of Entry (GPE) in accordance with RFO Subpart 5.1, unless an exception applies; 2. Solicit quotations from at least three sources; and 3. Whenever practicable, solicit quotations from two sources not included in the previous solicitation. Accordingly, the Government intends to solicit quotations directly from a minimum of three qualified sources. In accordance with RFO 5.201(b)(2), this presolicitation notice is being posted to the GPE in lieu of posting the solicitation itself to the GPE. The RFQ will be provided directly to the sources selected for solicitation. INTERESTED SOURCES Interested, responsible sources that wish to be considered for this requirement may submit the following information: - Company name; - Unique Entity Identifier (UEI); - Business size and socioeconomic status; - Point of contact, telephone number, and email address; and - A brief statement demonstrating the firm's capability to perform the required services briefly described above. Interested firms should submit this information to Contracting Office Joahnne Ongjoco by email at Joahnne_Ongjoco@ios.doi.gov no later than the response date and time listed above. The Government may use responses to this notice to identify additional qualified sources for direct solicitation. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR QUOTATION (RFQ). This presolicitation notice is for informational and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation, request for quotation, or commitment by the Government to award a contract. The Government will issue the RFQ directly to selected sources in accordance with RFO 12.201-1(c)(2). All responsible sources responding to this notice will be considered by the Government in determining the sources to be solicited.

title: Accommodations - Eloy, Arizona
description: The Department of National Defence (DND), on behalf of the Canadian Forces School of Search and Rescue (CFSSAR), requires hotel accommodation services in Eloy, Arizona, to support parachute training activities from 23 November to 5 December 2026 and 27 March to 24 April 2027. Accommodation must include single and double occupancy rooms, Wi-Fi, housekeeping services, laundry facilities, on-site parking, fitness facilities, breakfast service, and access to cooking facilities. Rooms must be non-smoking and include private washrooms, air conditioning, refrigerators, televisions, and workstations. During the Para Phase (March-April 2027), accommodation providers must be able to ensure complete separation between CFSSAR staff and students through separate buildings or controlled, physically separated areas. Further details are contained within the solicitation documents.

title: 6835--BULK OXYGEN - Bridge
description: This Special Notice of Intent (NOI) is not a request for competitive proposals.� This is not a solicitation or request for offers. � The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Loma Linda Healthcare System (LLHCS), intends to award a delivery order on a sole source basis to the incumbent RCG of North Carolina, LLC for the provision of bulk medical oxygen, including delivery, rental of the main storage tank, and rental of the backup tank. The previous contract option period was not exercised within the required timeframe, resulting in the facility relying on short term, month to month purchase orders to prevent disruption of service. Bulk medical oxygen is mission critical for patient care, life sustaining equipment, and overall hospital operations. Any lapse in supply would pose unacceptable risks to patient safety. This bridge acquisition is required to maintain uninterrupted oxygen delivery while the Department completes the necessary acquisition documentation and conducts competitive procurement for a long term follow on contract. This action is being taken pursuant to FAR 13.106 1(b), which permits sole source awards when the contracting officer determines that only one source is reasonably available. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 325120. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 6835. Any response to this notice must show clear and convincing evidence that competition would be advantageous to the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct competitive procurement. � A decision by the Government not to conduct competitive procurement for the proposed order based upon response to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. All inquiries shall be submitted via email to Anthony.delacruz@va.gov.

title: Medicaid Data Analysis for Bacterial Respiratory Pathogens and Information Systems
description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) awarded a sole source contract with MATHEMATICA INC., 1100 1ST ST NE FL 12, WASHINGTON, DC. 20002 This notice is provided in accordance with RFO FAR 8.401 & GSAM/R 538.7104-3(b)(1) . Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, National Center for Immunization and Respiratory Diseases, Division of Bacterial Diseases (DBD) requires support Services with the contractor listed above. The requested contractor Mathematica qualified as �innovator status� vendor for data analysis by Center for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS). Mathematica also has demonstrated experience and specialized staff with unique access and analytical capabilities for Medicaid data sets which captures the largest segment of US healthcare data, including births. The contractor shall perform analyses across four technical dimensions defined in the Statement of Work: (1) validating infant GBS case counts using TAF OT claims and evaluating a fourth case definition tied to maternal Medicaid IDs; (2) developing and refining a probabilistic mother-infant linkage algorithm using the Medicaid Case Number and supplementary variables; (3) estimating maternal vaccination coverage (COVID-19, influenza, Tdap, and prospectively RSV) accounting for bundled payment code effects; and (4) applying methods to reduce gestational age missingness using prenatal claims data. These tasks require continuity with linkage algorithms and case-definition logic Mathematica has already built and validated under prior CDC task orders. The authority permitting other than full and open competition is Title III of the Federal Property and Administrative Services Act of 1949 (41 U.S.C. 251, et seq.); Title 40 U.S.C. 501, Services for Executive Agencies, as implemented at FAR 8.401 and GSAM/R 538.7104-3(b)(1) "Only one source is capable of providing the products, services, or solution required at the level of quality required because the products, services, or solutions are unique or highly specialized." Through its prior contracts, Mathematica has already built key parts of this analysis�including updating the medical codes used to identify cases, working to link mother and infant records more completely, and adjusting for how individual states handle Medicaid enrollment for newborns. This steady, hands-on progress means Mathematica starts this next phase of work already ahead, with the knowledge and tools in place that a new contractor would not have. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation to Robin C. Meyer, Contract Specialist, at rcm2@cdc.gov, which shall be considered by the agency. The deadline for submissions is Ocotber 31, 2026 at 4:30PM EST. The Government will review any/all information submitted to determine if other responsible sources exist that could provide this requirement. Information received in response to this announcement will be used solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement.

description: The Federal Prison Industries (FPI) intends to solicit and award a competitively negotiated Architect and Engineer (A&E) Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ), Multiple Award Contract needed for new construction, renovation, alteration and repairs. The Architect and Engineer (A&E) shall furnish professional architectural, engineering, and related technical services, as specified herein, to the United States Government, Department of Justice, Federal Prison Industries (FPI). All work performed under this contract shall pertain to projects located at FPI facilities within the contiguous United States. In accordance with the Brooks Architect-Engineer Act, award(s) shall be made to the successful firm(s) based on demonstrated competence and qualifications to perform the services at fair and reasonable prices. Prior to this solicitation issuance, technical evaluations were conducted. This solicitation was then issued to the most highly rated firm(s). Therefore, in response to the solicitation, consideration for a contract award will be based solely upon the hourly rates, overhead and profit that are proposed and found to be fair and reasonable. Offerors are advised that award maybe made without discussions. Therefore, the initial proposal should provide sufficient information to recommend award without discussions and should reflect the offeror�s ability to perform at a reasonable price.

title: WIRING SYSTEM REPAIR SET FOR THE V-22 AIRCRAFT (FMS)
description: The Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWC-AD) is releasing Request for Quote (RFQ) N6833526Q1193 on a competitive basis for a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract to procure Peculiar Support Equipment (PSE), as detailed in the attached solicitation and associated documents. These PSE items are required to support the V-22 program. This solicitation is being issued as a 100% Small Business Set-Aside in accordance with FAR Part 19. Technical Data Package and Export Control Requirements: This solicitation includes DFARS 252.204-7025, Notice of Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) Requirements. The technical data package contains Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI). Offerors must obtain access to the CUI drawing package to prepare a proposal. Proof of CMMC Level 2 (Self) Assessment certification is required to request access to the technical data package. Refer to Section A of the solicitation document for full instructions regarding CMMC. The Government owns the Build-to-Print Technical Drawing Package, which is considered Export Controlled. All Offerors must possess a current and certified DD Form 2345 (Militarily Critical Technical Data Agreement) to request access to the drawings. Drawings will be provided to the designated data custodian listed on the certified DD Form 2345 via the DoD SAFE website. Refer to Section A of the solicitation document for full instructions regarding DD Form 2345. Requesting Access to Solicitation Documents: To request access to the Government-provided documents associated with this solicitation, Offerors must submit the following via email: 1. Proof of current and valid CMMC Level 2 (Self-Assessment) certification. 2. A certified DD Form 2345. Requests should be sent to the Point of Contact (POC) listed below. Solicitation Number: N6833526Q1133 Point of Contact and Questions The Point of Contact (POC) for this solicitation is: Eric Glawson, eric.j.glawson.civ@us.navy.mil and Kelli Ryan, kelli.l.ryan3.civ@us.navy.mil. All questions and inquiries regarding this solicitation must be submitted via email and reference Solicitation Number: N6833526Q1183 , Solicitation Title: WIRING SYSTEM REPAIR SET FOR THE V-22 AIRCRAFT (FMS) . Offerors are encouraged to review the solicitation and attachments thoroughly before submitting questions or requests for access. This RFQ shall not be construed as obligating the Government to award a contract or authorizing work to commence and shall not serve as a basis for any future claims against the Government.

title: Leather Sheepskin Hair Type
description: Defense Logistics Agency Troop Support (DLATS), Clothing & Textiles (C&T) Directorate, is conducting research to determine industry capabilities for Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type. This is a Sources Sought only and not a solicitation for proposals. This announcement is considered Market Research in accordance with FAR 10. DLA is the Defense Department�s principal buyer of multiple items within the Clothing & Textile industry that uses Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type. Numerous item specifications utilize Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type as a component in a wide variety of items purchased by DLA Troop Support, such as AR/PD 12-01 with Change 8 Amendment 1 and AR/PD 17-06 with Amendment 3, for Helmet Retention Systems. The primary purpose of this announcement is to identify potential sources with domestic manufacturing capabilities of Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type. This announcement also seeks to determine the availability of Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type production capacity, limitations and challenges. Domestic sources using Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type with domestic manufacturing capabilities are required in accordance with DFARS 252.225-7002-2(c) Preference for Certain Domestic Commodities (DEC 2017) All potential sources will be U.S. based. Additional market research may be conducted prior to posting any solicitation. The Government will not pay for any information received in response to this Sources Sought, nor will the Government compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing the information provided to the Government. This Source Sought does not constitute a commitment from the Government and any information provided in response to this Sources Sought will be used for informational purposes only. Any proprietary information submitted will be protected if appropriately marked. Vendor participation is not a promise for future business with the Government. The information for the below items is provided for informational purposes. It is highly recommended that vendors review the technical documents for items you can support then decide to request specifications. Vendors should use the following link to request item Specification: https://www.dla.mil/TroopSupport/ClothingandTextiles/SpecRequest.aspx Please use the contract opportunity notice ID �Sources Sought Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type� to obtain access. Fill in the request for the Technical Package requirements needed and under Special Instructions annotate �URGENT � MARKET RESEARCH � EXPEDITE.� The applicable North American Industrial Classification System Code (NAICS) is 315990 Apparel Accessories and Other Apparel Manufacturing. Small business size standards matched to industry NAICS codes are published by the Small Business Administration and are available at http://www.sba.gov/content/table-small-business-size-standards. Contractors must be registered with the Central Contractor Registration (CCR) at System for Award Management (SAM) http://www.sam.gov to be eligible for an award. Representations and certifications must also be on record. Submission requirements: Responses to this Sources Sought must be sent to Ryan Reynolds Contract Specialist, via email at Ryan.Reynolds@dla.mil and to Michelle Falkowski, Contracting Officer, via email at Michelle.Falkowski@dla.mil by the response date in this notice and should include company name, CAGE code, company size/profile, any other supportive information and answers to the below questions for each item for which you are potentially interested in supplying/supporting. 1. What is the absolute minimum quantity required for Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type? 2. What is your monthly minimum and maximum production capacity? 3. What is your current and maximum production rate of yards per week? 4. What is the minimum monthly production quantity required to be economically producible? 5. What is your available operating capacity at present? 6. What is the availability of the local labor pool? 7. Provide your Production Lead Time (PLT) for Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type. 8. Are there any issues with the availability of raw materials? 9. Please provide a summary of your current supply situation in terms of raw materials including major components, critical materials, lead-time issues, and suppliers. 10. Are you a supplier, distributor, contractor, or other of Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type? 11. What is the country of origin of Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type from your company? 12. In what country is your CAGE/NCAGE associated? Any information provided is voluntary.

title: Majoitus-, ravintola- ja ryhmätilapalvelut Reumaliiton järjestämille Arkea tukeville -kursseille
description: Majoitus-, ravintola- ja ryhmätilapalvelut Reumaliiton järjestämille Arkea tukeville -kursseille Hankinnan kohteena on Suomen Reumaliitto ry:n järjestämien Arkea tukevien -kurssien majoitus-, ruokailu- ja ryhmätilapalvelut. Hankinta koskee vuosina 2027 ja 2028 järjestettäviä kursseja. Lisäksi on mahdollisuus kahteen (2) optiovuoteen. Tarjouksia pyydetään kuudelta alueelta: Keski-Suomi, Pirkanmaa, Pohjois-Pohjanmaa, Pohjois-Savo, Päijät-Häme ja Helsinki-Uusimaa. Kursseja järjestetään vuosittain kahdeksan (8) valtakunnallisesti eri paikkakunnilla tilaajan määrittämällä tavalla. Kurssit ovat kestoltaan kahdesta vuorokaudesta (perjantaista - sunnuntaihin) neljään vuorokauteen (maanantaista -perjantaihin). Kursseilla on 16 -18 henkilöä. Kurssit on tarkoitettu aikuisille henkilöille, joilla on reuma tai muu tuki- ja liikuntaelinsairaus. Kurssipaikan majoitus-, ryhmä- ja ravintolatilojen tulee olla esteettömiä, jotta liikuntarajoitteiset henkilöt pystyvät toimimaan niissä. Invahuoneita tulee olla kahdesta kolmeen (2–3) kappaletta. Kurssipaikalle tulee voida saapua ja poistua julkisilla yhteyksillä, joiden pysäkki tai asema on enintään 500 metrin päässä kurssipaikasta (tai tarjoajan on mahdollista järjestää kuljetus kauempana olevalta pysäkiltä tai asemalta). Kaksi kursseista on luontopainotteisia, joten pihapiiristä tai lähiympäristöstä tulee löytyä helposti saavutettavia ja esteettömiä luontoreittejä. Kurssit järjestetään Sosiaali- ja terveysjärjestöjen avustuskeskuksen (STEA) myöntämällä valtionavustuksella. Hankittavan palvelun laajuus ja määrä perustuvat tulevan valtionavustuksen suuruuteen. Vuodelle 2027 myönnettävä valtionavustuksen määrä vahvistuu alkuvuodesta 2027. Hankinnan kohde ja sitä koskevat vaatimukset kuvataan tarkemmin liitteissä.,

title: Kannuksen Teollisuuskylä Oy:n teollisuushalli Raonhaka 1
description: Kannuksen Teollisuuskylä Oy:n teollisuushalli Raonhaka 1 Kannuksen Teollisuuskylä Oy on Kannuksen kaupungin ja kehitysyhtiö YritysKannuksen omistama kiinteistökehitysyhtiö, jonka toiminnan tavoitteena on mahdollistaa kohtuuhintaisia teollisia kasvutiloja yrityksille Kannuksessa. Yhtiö hakee nyt seuraavalle hallihankkeelle edullista ja laadukasta hallivalmistajaa, joka toimii samalla hankkeen pääurakoijana. Pääurakoijan vastuulle kuuluu myös kohteen rakennesuunnittelu. Hankkeen tekniset ratkaisut pyritään tekemään siten, että lopputuloksena valmistuu laadukasta, mutta mahdollisimman kustannustehokasta toimintatilaa vuokralaisena toimiville teollisuusyrityksille. Pääsuunnittelun on toteuttanut Arkkitehtitoimisto Paloranta Oy, LVISA-suunnittelusta vastaa Ratech Oy. Kannuksen Raonhaan teollisuusalueelle suunniteltu noin 1000 m2 teollisuushalli toteutetaan kahdessa osassa. Tässä tarjouspyynnössä pyydetään tarjoamaan nyt rakennettavan neljän lohkon kokonaisuuden kokonaishinta, sekä mahdollisten lisätöiden tuntihinta. Ensimmäiset neljä lohkoa rakennetaan piirustusten mukaisesti ensin, loput kaksi lohkoa laajennetaan heti, kun rakennettavat tilat on saatu täytettyä vuokralaisilla. Rakentaminen on tarkoitus aloittaa välittömästi, pohjatyöt pyritään saamaan valmiiksi ennen talvea, hallin pystytys ja varustelu talven aikana, käyttöönotto mahdollisimman nopeasti keväällä 2027. Laajennuksen rakentamisen aikataulua ei ole määritelty, mutta rakentaminen pyritään toteuttamaan saman pääurakoitsijan kanssa. Laajennuksen toteutuksessa käytetään tämän tarjouskilpailun hintaa, joka sidotaan kuitenkin laajennuksen osalta yleiseen kustannusindeksiin. Laajennuksen toteutuksesta laaditaan tulevaisuudessa oma sopimus ja aikataulu. Hankkeen käytännön toteutus on kuvattu Urakkaohjelmassa. Salassapito ja muut hankintaa koskevat seikat YSE 1998 mukaisesti. Tarjouksen vähimmäisvaatimukset, hylkäämisperusteet ja pisteytys on kuvattu omassa dokumentissaan.,

title: Industry Day: A Government-Industry Exchange on Construction Contracting - An Invitation for Industry Partners to Collaborate with the United States Space Force Operational Contracting Enterprise
description: Industry teammates, the Senior Contracting Official (SCO) for Operational and Enterprise Space Contracting invites you to a pivotal event discussing the future of construction in the U.S. Space Force. We are creating a forum to hear industry concerns and clarify the purpose of these new authorities to move faster, not to limit competition or replace valuable tools like Multiple Award Construction Contracts (MACCs). We have been granted new, flexible authorities for construction contracting, including Other Transaction Authority (OTA) under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a, and we want to partner with you to redefine how we build for the future. Join Us To: Hear directly from the SCO on the commitment to a fair, transparent, and collaborative construction process. Understand the New Authorities - A clear breakdown of what Construction OTAs are (and what they aren't), the 2808a authority, and how these tools fit into the broader acquisition landscape. Teach Us - This is an opportunity for industry to educate the government on commercial construction best practices and innovative methods to go from concept to capability � faster. Event Details: Date: 14 September 2026 Time: 0900-1200 (General Session); 1300-1400 (One on One Sessions) Location: Innovation Hub, 2424 Garden of the Gods Rd, Colorado Springs, CO (Will also be presented on Microsoft Teams) Who Should Attend? This event is for members of the construction industry, specifically general contractors, to come together to discuss, the Department of the Air Force (USAF & USSF) contracting processes including the new authorities and how we can work better with industry partners to achieve a more efficient means of awarding projects. Limited to two personnel per company. Registration Form: https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/w3yV4dh0zp

buyer: Permanent Secretariat of the Transport Community
title: Serbia – Development consultancy services – Study on the Availability, Quality and EU Compliance of TEN-T Rest Areas, Safe and Secure Truck Parking Areas in the Western Balkans
description: The Permanent Secretariat of the Transport Community aims to conclude a service contract for preparation of the Study whose primary aim is to review the transposition of the TEN-T Regulation 1679/2024 in the Western Balkans region and to assess the current availability, quality, and compliance with the relevant EU legislation regarding the rest areas (RAs) and safe and secure parking areas (SSTPAs) along the Trans-European Transport Network (TEN-T) in the Western Balkans. The Study will deliver an inventory of RAs and SSTPAs along the TEN-T network (including border crossing points) in the Western Balkans populating TODIS (Transport Observatory Database/Information System) with these data, assessing their compliance with EU safety, security, and service standards. It will identify critical gaps, evaluate future demand, and provide policy, technical and investment recommendations for infrastructure upgrades. Furthermore, it will outline key findings and an action plan for implementation, supporting alignment with TEN-T requirements and enhancing road transport efficiency and safety. This Study could be helpful in situation that some of Western Balkans Regional Partners do not have defined locations and reserved spaces for RAs and SSTPAs within their spatial planning documentation. This Study will also enhance regulatory alignment with EU policies and practices. Specific tasks, deliverables, and requirements will be detailed and described in the Tender Specifications.

title: Sweden – Transport services (excl. Waste transport) – Bussresor
description: Del 1: Uppdraget avser busstransporter med busstorlek högst 22 passagerare och busstorlek över 22 passagerare och högst 55 passagerare. För elever i grundskolan är det i första hand badskjutsar tur och retur från skola till badhus (Navet) som efterfrågas. Badskjutsar är schemalagda, nya scheman skickas ut innan varje terminsstart. Resor föranledda av skolornas aktiviteter t.ex. resor till utbildning i andra skolor inom Umeå kommun, utflykter, skolresor och vid evakueringar när det sker ombyggnader av skolor. Vid badskjutsar ska avlämning ske 10 minuter före badtid, hämtning ska ske 20 minuter efter badtid om inte annan överenskommelse görs mellan parterna. Schema bifogas Del1.1: Uppdraget består resor beställda av verksamheter inom kommunen och övriga medverkande i upphandlingen som t.ex. vid konferenser, informationsdagar eller liknande och det kan vara resor över dagen eller resor med övernattningar. Bussar som ska användas i uppdraget ska vara anpassade för uppdragets utförande och inte vara större fordon än resan kräver. Del 2: Uppdraget avser busstransporter med 1 buss max 55 passagerare. Normalt sett används en buss men vid undantagsfall kan flera bussar krävas samtidigt. Kulturskolan bokar resor för såväl kommunala som fristående skolor och förskolor för transporter till/från kulturevenemang. Med kulturevenemang menas teater- och dansföreställningar, museibesök, biblioteksaktiviteter, konserter etc. Kulturbussen skjutsar inte till idrottsevent, friluftsdagar, simhall eller andra skolaktiviteter. Kulturbussen skjutsar förskolegrupper och klasser enbart inom Umeå kommun och kommundelar, enbart under skoltid 08.30-15.30. Kulturbussen bokas minst 10 dagar innan resan ska genomföras. Planering görs av kulturskolan terminsvis.

title: SOFTWARE LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: CorrelateIQ - Correlation-Based System Intelligence
description: CorrelateIQ reveals hidden relationships among many data streams at once, catching hidden patterns, early warning signs and operating shifts that single-variable monitoring overlooks. Built on analysis techniques from high-energy physics, this software from Los Alamos National Laboratory turns existing sensor and process data into practical insight that helps organizations prevent failures, protect quality and reduce downtime. Because the method makes no assumptions about where the data comes from, it applies to a wide range of numeric data, from manufacturing sensors and equipment logs to financial records, market data and scientific measurements. Overview Factories, laboratories, infrastructure networks, financial and real-estate markets now produce huge volumes of linked data from sensors, equipment logs and transactions. Most analytics tools, however, judge each variable separately or depend on fixed thresholds that trigger an alert only after a single reading crosses a limit. These methods have trouble spotting effects that arise from subtle interactions among many variables, such as gradual equipment wear, a drifting manufacturing process or a market entering a new phase. As a result, organizations often miss the earliest warning signals, react to failures only after they happen and leave much of the value in their data untapped. Teams in every data-reach fields need a practical way of understanding how an entire system behaves as a whole, not merely how each part performs alone. Key Benefits Spots early warning signs before small problems become costly failures Uncovers the hidden factors that drive outcomes such as quality, risk or price Reveals relationships across many data sources that conventional tools miss Identifies which combinations of variables matter most Gets more value from data organizations already collect Works across industries and data types, from factory sensors to financial records Condenses complex, high-volume data into clear, compact indicators Complements existing monitoring, machine learning and digital twin systems Core Capabilities At its core, CorrelateIQ: Correlation-Based System Intelligence measures collective behavior. Users choose the variables or signals of interest, and the software calculates higher-order correlations that capture how those inputs change together rather than separately. The framework accepts mixed data types, including time-series records, sensor readings, transactional data and scientific measurements. It condenses them into compact representations of overall system behavior. Because the software reduces many interacting variables to a smaller set of meaningful indicators, complex environments become easier to read, compare and act upon. CorrelateIQ also goes beyond a single snapshot. It tracks how correlation patterns change over time, so users can see shifts in operating state, new anomalies and transitions from one regime to another. Its outputs can act as an analytics or feature-generation layer that feeds existing monitoring, control or machine learning systems. It can run in real-time monitoring pipelines or offline analytics platforms. Planned improvements include automated selection and ranking of the most useful correlations, adaptive correlation building and closer integration with predictive maintenance and digital twin workflows. Use Cases & Market Applications Semiconductor and advanced manufacturing (process monitoring, quality control) Industrial operations and energy (predictive maintenance, equipment health) Infrastructure (structural health monitoring, multisensor networks) Industrial software and digital twins (system modeling, feature generation) Finance and real estate (market shift detection, risk analysis) Scientific research (physics data analysis, complex systems studies) Healthcare, transportation and cybersecurity (anomaly detection, early warning) Supply chains and climate monitoring (leading indicators, change detection) LA-UR-26-29216 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. LANL�s licensing program focuses on moving inventions developed by our researchers to commercial innovations. Patented and patent pending inventions and copyrighted software are available to existing and start-up companies through exclusive and non-exclusive licensing agreements. For specific discussions, please contact licensing@lanl.gov.
